Class Main

java.lang.Object
Main
public class Main extends Object
Entry point for concurrent dataset standardization using a CyclicBarrier.

Standardizing data (z-score normalization) rescales each value to (value - mean) / standard deviation, a common preprocessing step before statistical analysis or machine learning: 

   z = (x - μ) / σ

Execution Workflow & Concurrency Design:

  • Data Partitioning: The dataset is partitioned into contiguous chunks, one per worker thread.
  • Phase 1 (partial sums): Each worker thread computes the sum of its assigned data chunk and stores the result in its dedicated index of the set of partial sums.
  • Barrier synchronization 1: Threads wait at barrier.await(). No thread can proceed to compute deviations until all threads have completed their partial sum calculations, ensuring the global mean (μ) can be computed.
  • Phase 2 (squared deviations): All threads read the set of partial sums to determine the global mean (μ) and compute the sum of squared deviations for their chunk, writing the result into a set of partial squares.
  • Barrier synchronization 2: Threads wait at the same barrier.await(). No thread can normalize its chunk until all threads have finished Phase 2, ensuring the global standard deviation (σ) can be computed.
  • Phase 3 (normalization): Each thread computes the global standard deviation and normalizes its chunk in place as (value - mean) / stdDev.

Key Concurrency Principles:

  • Why barriers are required: The global mean depends on every chunk, and the standard deviation depends on the global mean. A thread that finished its own chunk cannot continue until all the others have finished too, so the algorithm has two synchronization points, and the same CyclicBarrier serves both.
  • Why join is not enough: The threads could be joined after each phase, and new ones started, but then each phase would pay for creating new threads and would lose the per-thread state (chunk and mean). A barrier lets the same threads continue to the next phase.
  • Lock-free safety: No locks are needed because each thread writes only its own slot of the set of partial sums and squares, and only its own data chunk. The barrier makes those writes visible to the other threads before anyone reads them.

  • Method Details

    • main

      public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException
      Application main entry point.

      Generates a synthetic dataset of values, coordinates parallel standardization across worker threads using a CyclicBarrier, and sequentially verifies that the normalized dataset has a mean of ~0 and standard deviation of ~1.

      Parameters:
      args - command-line arguments (not used)
      Throws:
      InterruptedException - if the main thread is interrupted while waiting for worker threads to finish
